solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Teases one's hair and rear with warm undergarments

parts.note: the back is the rear
combs, short for combinations, are an old one-piece woollen undergarment

explanation.surface: Someone fusses with their hair and their bottom while wearing thermal underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Combinations, or combs, are an old-fashioned all-in-one undergarment covering body and legs.
explanation.definitionFit: To backcomb is to comb hair towards the scalp to give it volume, which is what teasing hair means.

clue.text: Go swimming at city close to seaside

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England

indicators.note: the close of something is its end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A visitor takes a swim in a town near the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath, a Somerset city famous for its Roman baths, also fits the swimming surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe can mean to take a swim in the sea or a river, an older British usage.

clue.text: Monks putting hat on scoundrels, right away

indicators.note: sending right away means removing the abbreviation for right from the word
putting one thing on another places them side by side, the first in front of the second

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat
urchins are mischievous young rascals

explanation.surface: Friars place hats on some rogues and then promptly leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The R of the rascals is removed before the hat goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Capuchins are friars of a Franciscan order named after their pointed hood.

clue.text: Artist having anonymous holiday home with horse said to be ten

indicators.note: anonymous means without a name, so the abbreviation for name is dropped

parts.note: a caravan is a mobile holiday home
gee-gee is baby talk for a horse

indicators.note: said means spoken out, so the number is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: ten written as figures is a one and a nought, which look like the letters

explanation.surface: A painter with a caravan and a horse claims to be a perfect ten.
explanation.walkthrough: Ten written 10 looks like the letters I and O; N for name goes from the holiday home.
explanation.definitionFit: Caravaggio was an Italian Baroque painter famous for dramatic light and shadow.

clue.text: Hash can appear in Tommy's!

parts.note: a mess, as in making a hash of something
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A soldier's stew may turn up in his kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy is the old nickname for a British private soldier. The whole clue also describes the item: hash, a stew, is served in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess tin is a soldier's metal eating container, the vessel a Tommy's hash would be served in.

clue.text: Escort to the door and shriek about a cry of pain

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to shout is to cry out loudly
ow is the exclamation of pain

explanation.surface: A host ushers someone out and yells at a painful cry.
explanation.definitionFit: To show someone out is to accompany them to the exit, the phrasal verb for escorting a guest away.

clue.text: Sound runner to the right and left

parts.note: a ski is a runner on snow, like a sledge runner
R is the standard abbreviation for right
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A sound engineer is told an athlete ran right and left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but here it is a ski, the runner a skier glides on.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirl is the shrill wailing noise made by bagpipes, so it is a particular kind of sound.

clue.text: House-builders' workplace isn't pleasant to see, we're told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: something unpleasant to look at is a sight, as in 'you look a sight'

explanation.surface: A building plot is an eyesore, so we hear.
explanation.definitionFit: A building site is where builders work, so house-builders' workplace describes a site.

clue.text: Become liable backing police force and its patch

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the combined letters are read from end to start

parts.note: the Royal Ulster Constabulary, the old Northern Ireland police
Northern Ireland, the area that force covered

explanation.surface: Someone takes responsibility for supporting a police force and its beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a debt or penalty is to become liable for it, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Oddly, no letter 'G' in eye-glass

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters that follow are set out in an unusual order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Strangely, the word for a monocle lacks a G.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like it selects odd letters; here it signals a rearrangement. The joke is that the answer does contain a G.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of spectacles held up to the eyes on a handle, an old kind of eyeglass.

clue.text: He drinks and is a bit blotto, personally

indicators.note: a bit is a piece of something, so the letters are a fragment taken from inside the following words

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A drinker admits he is somewhat drunk himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Blotto is slang for very drunk, which suits the surface nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: A toper is a habitual heavy drinker, a man described simply by the fact that he drinks.

clue.text: Son left mark with his Porsche?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
port is the left side of a ship
a scar is a mark left on skin

explanation.surface: A son crashed and scratched his Porsche, leaving a mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left mark' reads as damage done, but left is the nautical side and mark a scar. The question mark flags the Porsche as only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Porsche is a high-performance motor car, a well-known example of the breed.

clue.text: Tax a novice arranging digs

indicators.note: arranging puts things into a fresh order, so the preceding letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A beginner is charged for sorting out their lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digs' looks like British slang for lodgings, but it is the plural noun for archaeological sites.
explanation.definitionFit: An excavation is an archaeological dig, so digs is the plural noun meaning the same thing.

clue.text: Smile, taking day off from hard work

indicators.note: taking something off removes it, here the abbreviation for day

parts.note: a grind is laborious work
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Someone smiles because they have a day's break from heavy work.
explanation.definitionFit: A grin is a broad smile, a close synonym for the noun.

clue.text: Instructions to patrol member receiving punishment

parts.note: a Girl Guide troop is split into patrols
lines are a school punishment of copying out a sentence many times

explanation.surface: Orders are given to a member of a patrol who is being disciplined.
explanation.walkthrough: Guides are the girls' scouting movement, organised in small patrols; lines are a British school punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Guidelines are rules or advice on how to act, so they are instructions.

clue.text: Confinement means rising late

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the old term for the period of childbirth
second meaning: staying in bed longer in the morning

explanation.surface: Being locked up means you get to sleep in.
explanation.walkthrough: Confinement here is the dated word for childbirth, not imprisonment.
explanation.definitionFit: A lying-in is an old name for childbirth and its rest period; lying in also describes staying in bed late.

clue.text: Drop in at the pub that's cheap telephonically

definitions.note: an adjective phrase standing for a noun: something cheap on the telephone

parts.note: the local is one's neighbourhood pub
to call is to pay a short visit

explanation.surface: Stopping by at the pub is an inexpensive outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At' places the visit after the pub. In Britain a local is the pub nearest home.
explanation.definitionFit: A local call is a telephone call within the same area, charged at the lowest rate.

clue.text: Elephant's call to Donald and alien

parts.note: Donald Trump, the US president
ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: An elephant calls out to Donald and to a creature from space.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpet is the loud cry an elephant makes through its trunk, an animal sound named after the instrument.

clue.text: F1 driver's speed — flat out

parts.note: Alain Prost, four-time Formula One champion
rate is a pace or speed

explanation.surface: A racing driver's pace is at its very maximum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat out' sounds like full speed after the racing words, but it means lying flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Prostrate means lying stretched out face down, which is lying flat out.

clue.text: Keep capturing leading Iberian kingdom

indicators.note: capturing means taking something in and holding it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle

indicators.note: leading means at the front, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fortress holds out against the foremost kingdom of the Iberian peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iberian kingdom' looks like the definition, and it fits, but the word Iberian is needed for its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Castile was a medieval kingdom in central Spain that later united with Aragon.

clue.text: Came out at end of soiree and mingled

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter
merged means mixed together

explanation.surface: A guest appeared towards the close of a party and circulated.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerged means appeared or came into view, the past tense matching came out.

clue.text: Dolores looking silly in pink

indicators.note: looking silly suggests something made foolish and disordered, so the name's letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman named Dolores looks foolish dressed in pink.
explanation.definitionFit: Old rose is a muted, greyish shade of pink, so it names one particular pink.

clue.text: Award includes university learner for kissing

definitions.note: a phrase standing for an adjective: relating to kissing

indicators.note: something that includes other things holds them inside it

parts.note: an Oscar is a film award
U is the abbreviation for university
L is for learner, from the L-plate

explanation.surface: A prize given to a student for romantic scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: U and L join and go inside the film award.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscular means relating to the mouth or to kissing, from the Latin osculum, a kiss.

clue.text: Regularly seen in sleazier dugout

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A seedier hideout is frequently spotted.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a den or hiding place, and a dugout is a shelter dug into the ground.

clue.text: Popular county ground, initially, without name

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
Co. is the abbreviation for county

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: A well-liked cricket county ground goes unnamed at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'County ground' reads as one sporting phrase but splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Incog is short for incognito, describing someone travelling under a hidden identity.

clue.text: Strains of carol Pete's arranged

indicators.note: a piece of music that is arranged is reworked, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Musical strains from a carol that Pete has arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strains' looks like a musical noun after the carol, but it is a verb, as in straining coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: To percolate is to pass a liquid through a filter, which is what straining it does.

clue.text: Water vapour from First Surrey eleven

indicators.note: first means the opening position, so only the initial letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter
a cricket or football side has eleven players

explanation.surface: Mist rises from the first eleven of Surrey county cricket club.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is an English county with a famous cricket club; a side of eleven is a team.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam is the gas water becomes when boiled, also called water vapour.

clue.text: Average out one and two

indicators.note: being out around something means lying outside it, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Two numbers averaged out give one and two.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is a set of two things, so the noun means the number two.

clue.text: Arab's loose coins left for messenger

parts.note: Ar is the dictionary abbreviation for Arabic or Arab
small change is loose coins
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An Arab's spare coins are left behind for a courier.
explanation.walkthrough: The word angel comes from the Greek for messenger, which makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: An archangel is a chief angel, and angels in scripture are God's messengers.

clue.text: Hymn writer will stoop to pray, we're told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to kneel is to bend down for prayer

explanation.surface: A hymn writer will bow down in prayer, so we hear.
explanation.walkthrough: John Mason Neale was a Victorian clergyman who wrote and translated many hymns, including Good King Wenceslas.
explanation.definitionFit: John Mason Neale was a prolific nineteenth-century English hymn writer and translator.

clue.text: Drink having the king's backing

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: regal means belonging to a king

explanation.surface: A beverage enjoys royal support.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light beer, a common kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Sad matter affected those on the oche

indicators.note: something affected is altered, so the preceding letters are changed in order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sorry business has upset the people standing at the line.
explanation.walkthrough: The oche is the line behind which darts players stand to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A darts team is a group of players who take turns throwing from behind the oche.
